executiveBoard.name: Mrs. Sally Stovall
executiveBoard.title: President
executiveBoard.bio:
Mrs. Sally Stovall is a passionate leader committed to advancing faith, unity, and cultural heritage within African Catholic communities. Since 2017, she has served as President of the National Association of African Catholics in the United States (NAACUS), guiding initiatives that strengthen evangelization, foster cultural identity, and build vibrant communities rooted in Catholic values. Her leadership reflects NAACUS's mission to unite African Catholics, promote spiritual growth, and celebrate diversity within the universal Church.

Sally's dedication extends beyond NAACUS. She contributes to the United States Conference of Catholic Bishops (USCCB) through the Pastoral Care for Migrants, Refugees, and Travelers (PCMRT) subcommittee and chaired the 2016 African National Eucharistic Congress (ANEC), a landmark event for African Catholics in the U.S. Locally, she co-founded the African Catholic Ministry in the Archdiocese of Indianapolis and led the Global Children African Dancers for 14 years, blending faith and culture through art.

Her service includes mentoring youth and young adults, supporting underrepresented communities, and promoting cultural initiatives nationally. A devoted parishioner, she served on her parish council and chaired the Finance Council for 17 years. Professionally, Sally is a banker with an MBA in Business Administration. She is married and a proud mother of two young adults. Her life embodies NAACUS's vision: inspiring others to live their faith fully while embracing cultural identity and community.

executiveBoard.name: Mr. Kwame Frimpong
executiveBoard.title: Vice President
executiveBoard.bio:
Kwame Frimpong is known for his passion for Pan Africanism – a solidly united Africa – and his love for Christ, and His love and mercy for humanity. He describes himself as an African Catholic.

This passion for Africanism and the acceptance of Christ's love and mercies has guided his growth to be committed and resolute towards African Catholicism. The early stages of life – in his 20s and 30s – were dedicated to assisting to form and inform the Catholic Youth in Ghana – from the parish level to the national level. Additionally, in this period, he was a prominent member of Pax Romana (IMCS) in the University, and Pax Romana (ICMICA) after college years.

His transition to the United States did not slow him down. His passion caught the eyes of his peers at the parish level, and they invited him to participate in the African Catholic Association of the DMV – a diocesan association. At this level, he assisted the then President, Dr. Seikor Bundu, to revitalize the association. This effort did not go unnoticed. Rev Sister Joanna Okereke, in her efforts to revamp NAACUS, appointed him as the Vice President to the association.

In NAACUS, he found fresh opportunities to work with his peers to know and love Christ more, and to brand themselves as African Catholics in a stronger aspect. As the appointed Vice President to NAACUS, he supports the able and willing President, Mrs. Sally Stovall, to move the Association to a higher level. He participates in the Constitution, Advocacy, Finance, Fundraising, Marketing, Public Relations, Resource, and Outreach ministries. In addition, he coordinates the activities of the Regional Coordinators and publishes the NAACUS Connection.

Currently, his passion in NAACUS is to identify and recruit persons who are willing to join the team, assist Madam President to bring them on board, and motivate and empower such peers to work in the Lord's vineyard.

To paraphrase the great legend Bob Marley, he says, how good and pleasant it will be before God and man to see the unification of our African brothers and sisters.

WE ARE CATHOLICS. WE ARE AFRICANS. WE ARE NAACUS. WE ARE TOGETHER.

executiveBoard.name: Mr. Alex Nana Boadi Danso
executiveBoard.title: General Secretary
executiveBoard.bio:
Alex Nana Boadi Danso is a Ghanaian Catholic living in Silver Spring, Maryland.

Nana is passionate about community life, and he takes delight in equipping his community members to share God's love and creating a welcoming community for all. Before becoming the current President of his Community in Takoma Park under the Archdiocese of Washington, Nana was the Catechist driven by the vision to help people to connect with the gospel in everyday life.

Nana has an insatiable desire to see all African Catholics coming together as a formidable front to spearhead the programs for, and advocate on behalf of all African Catholics in the United States. As the current General Secretary of NAACUS, he executes his duties with passion, and he is very active and serves on other Ministries.

Before joining the NAACUS Team, Nana attended University of Science and Technology in Ghana, Aalborg University in Denmark, and University of Maryland, USA.

He is the founder and Principal Broker for Lexidan Realty & Development Services.

executiveBoard.name: Sr. Dr. Maddy Claire Takyala
executiveBoard.title: Assistant General Secretary
executiveBoard.bio:
Sr. Dr. Maddy Takyala is the current Assistant Secretary General of NAACUS. She is a religious sister in the Daughters of Mary congregation. She gives talks and seminars on spiritual responsiveness and the harmonious integration of faith, reason, and technology in the education system, leadership, and church.

Additionally, she is the author of several articles and works, including "Burliness and Epitome of a Woman": An Analytical Leadership Lens of Female Bible Characters (Eve, Sarah, And Deborah), All in One Microsoft Processing, Takyala Leadership Style, Takyala Leadership Reflection Questions, and Luganda-English Folktales: Engero Ensonge Mu Luganda N'oluzungu.

executiveBoard.name: Reine Marie Assana
executiveBoard.title: Assistant Public Relations Officer
executiveBoard.bio:
Reine Assana is a Senegalese immigrant currently residing in the Archdiocese of Milwaukee, Wisconsin. She serves as the Assistant Public Relations Officer for NAACUS. She is a widowed parent of three beautiful daughters and a young man. Born and raised in the Catholic faith, she is a devoted Catholic.

In her role, Reine works closely with the Public Relations Officer to ensure that information about all NAACUS activities and events is widely spread in our communities and beyond. In collaboration with the IT section, she also works to ensure that our website reflects who we are in terms of content. She serves as a liaison with regional coordinators to gather information about the various events happening in our various communities.

Reine is currently working for Waste Management Inc. as a Technical Service Representative, handling the Canadian market area. She has a passion for the African community and fosters collaboration between African communities both in the Church and outside the Church. Because of her widespread connections in various communities in the area, NAACUS organized its 2nd regional conference in Milwaukee, Wisconsin in July of 2022.

She is a member of the Black Commission of the Archdiocese of Milwaukee.

Together we shine: Matthew 5:14-16 ("Let your light shine") — Please join us with NAACUS as we shine the light of Christ in a world full of darkness.

executiveBoard.name: Sr. Henrietta Okoro HHCJ
executiveBoard.title: Treasurer
executiveBoard.bio:
I am Sister Henrietta Okoro, a devout member of the Congregation of Handmaids of the Holy Child Jesus (HHCJ). It is with great joy and humility that I share my journey within this cherished religious community. On October 7th, 1989, I made my first religious profession of vows, dedicating my life to the service of God and the mission of my congregation.

As a life member of the Handmaids of the Holy Child Jesus (HHCJ), I am privileged to possess an active voice within my community, holding the invaluable rights to vote and to be voted for. These rights are a testament to the deep trust and collective responsibility I share as a family devoted to the teachings and values of my faith.

In all humility, I embrace my role within the HHCJ family, standing steadfast in my commitment to our shared mission and the spiritual journey we undertake together. My life is a testament to the enduring bonds of faith, service, and devotion that unite us as Handmaids of the Holy Child Jesus.

My educational journey includes earning my Associate Science in Nursing (ASN) Degree in 2011 and a Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) Degree in 2012 from the College of Saint Mary in Omaha, Nebraska. In 2017, I received a Master's Degree in Nursing Science and Clinical Nurse Leadership from Sacred Heart University in Fairfield, Connecticut.

I have a diverse nursing background, including experience in medical/surgical, geriatric, orthopedic, plastic, oral maxilla and facial, bariatric, and obstetric/oncology nursing.

By God's grace I am the National Treasurer for the National Association of African Catholics in the United States. May my continued service to the church be a source of grace and inspiration to all those I encounter on my spiritual path. To God be the glory. In faith and love.

executiveBoard.name: Deacon Francis Nyawello M. Chan
executiveBoard.title: Financial Secretary
executiveBoard.bio:
Deacon Francis Nyawello M. Chan serves in the Diocese of Des Moines, Iowa. He holds the positions of NAACUS Financial Secretary and National Advisor for Sudanese and South Sudanese American Catholics in the USA.

Deacon Francis Chan holds a Bachelor's degree in Theology and a Master of Arts in Pastoral Studies. Originally from East Africa - South Sudan, he is now a U.S. citizen. He was ordained a permanent deacon 19 years ago with the Diocese of Des Moines, Iowa, and is a member of African Catholic clergy and religious women in the U.S.

Deacon Chan is assigned to St. Ambrose Cathedral parish in Des Moines, where he serves among over five different nationalities and several different ministries in his capacity as deacon of the church, particularly among Sudanese and South Sudanese Catholics in the USA.

Deacon Francis Chan founded a group called Catholics Warriors, which helps encourage Sudanese and South Sudanese Catholics who left the church to come back home to mother church through singing in Arabic and other languages spoken in Sudan and South Sudan. This group celebrates every feast day of two Sudanese saints, Daniel Comboni and Josephine Bakhita, with celebrations moving from state to state every year.

Deacon Francis Chan also serves as assistant coordinator for the refugee community at the diocesan level.

ministryCoordinations.name: Mrs. Ifeoma (Ify) Uzoh-Anigbogu
ministryCoordinations.title: Women's Ministry Coordinator
ministryCoordinations.bio: Dr. Ifeoma Uzoh-Anigbogu is a dedicated wife and mother of three, and the Coordinator of NAACUS Women's Ministry. She is a Healthcare professional with a strong interest in mental health and holistic well-being, as well as a business owner. She is deeply committed to her Christian faith. She is passionate about service, leadership, and fostering spiritual growth while meeting people with compassion and understanding. Above all, she loves the things of God and is committed to building strong women of faith, fostering unity, and inspiring others to serve God and humanity with love, dedication and purpose.

ministryCoordinations.name: Dr. Juliet Njoku
ministryCoordinations.title: Youth Ministry Coordinator
ministryCoordinations.bio:
Dr. Juliet Njoku, a Senior Judicial Officer with the Superior Court of New Jersey, Gloucester County since 2002, has made significant contributions to her community. She served as a member of the EEO/AA Advisory Board of New Jersey Judiciary in her Vicinage. Additionally, she has been a member of Pi Alpha Alpha National Honor Society for Public Affairs & Administration since 2015.

Dr. Juliet is deeply committed to her Catholic faith. She is an Associate of the Society of the Holy Child Jesus (SHCJ) and a member of the Racial Justice Commission, Camden Diocese, since 2010. Furthermore, she serves as the vice chair of the Pastoral Council in her parish. Dr. Juliet actively participates in the African/Igbo Catholic communities in Camden Diocese, coordinating the participation of African/Igbo Catholic youths at various Diocesan and National Youth events.

Dr. Juliet's dedication extends to her role as a Board Member/Regional Coordinator of the National Association of African Catholics in the United States (NAACUS) since 2018. In 2019, she co-chaired and organized the inaugural NAACUS Regional Conference in Trenton, New Jersey. Currently, she serves as the coordinator of the Youth Ministry for NAACUS and has successfully organized several virtual Zoom youth events featuring renowned speakers and presenters.

Dr. Juliet actively engages with the diaspora community in the greater Philadelphia area. She serves as a Board Member of FunTimes Magazine Philadelphia, a publication that celebrates the African diaspora. Since 2024, she has been the Chairlady of the Nigerian American Mothers for Youth Advancement USA (NAMYAUSA), a prominent professional organization for Nigerian women in the tri-state region. In 2023, she joined the Delaware Africa Coalition and currently serves on its Public Relations Committee. Dr. Juliet finds joy in meditation, reading, organizing, traveling, and embarking on adventures.

ministryCoordinations.name: Stella Bello
ministryCoordinations.title: Fundraising Coordinator
ministryCoordinations.bio:
Stella Bello (Mrs), NAACUS Fundraising Coordinator. Stella Bello is originally from Nigeria, currently living in Maryland. She is an Oncology clinical social worker and Oncology Patient Financial Navigator.

She has a background and experience in raising funds and chairing various harvest and church building committees, having worked as three times Harvest financial chairperson, two times Church building financial chair person, and also chairing other fundraising organizations. She is currently Oncology social worker/ Patient financial navigator, ensuring that finance does not become barriers to care, apart from providing psychosocial support. Her ability to drive strategic initiatives has helped secure millions in funding and transform communities from one project at a time, e..g church building, Priest residence, ensuring that uninsured cancer patients, cancer patients living below poverty get care, regardless of the cost.

As Fundraising Coordinator, she plans to serve NAACUS with the support of others , by soliciting and raising funds.

Her passion for NAACUS is her desire to uplift African American Catholics through trusted, spiritual and culturally competent leadership seeing African Americans speak with one voice in unity and love.

Stella Bello appreciates team work, welcomes ideas, conversations on how NAACUS can be better served, and achieves its goals. She looks forward to working with innovative minds. You can reach out to her anytime.

ministryCoordinations.name: Dr. Florence Njoyi
ministryCoordinations.title: Outreach Ministry Coordinator
ministryCoordinations.bio:
Dr. Florence Njoyi is a dedicated practicing Catholic and a distinguished multicultural behavioral health clinician, boasting over twenty years of experience, originating from Cameroon, West Africa. As a committed member of the Catholic faith, she places significant importance on Catholic education, practices, and community support in nurturing spiritual growth.

Her leadership within Catholic groups is characterized by compassion and a profound commitment to fostering unity, which has enriched the cultural heritage of African Catholic practices. This has created a vibrant tapestry of faith that resonates with individuals from diverse backgrounds. Through her innovative programs and unwavering dedication, she has cultivated environments where cultural expression and spiritual growth coexist harmoniously, empowering individuals to celebrate their unique identities while contributing to the broader Church community.

As a dedicated member of the Catholic Women's Association (CWA), Cameroon, USA, Fellowship Small Groups and National Association of African Catholics in the United States (NAACUS), she promotes understanding and inclusivity within U.S. African Catholic communities. In her various roles, she has spearheaded initiatives that encourage dialogue and respect among different cultures, ensuring that all voices are valued. Her programs assist African Catholics in their spiritual journeys and empower women within the Catholic Women's Association to take on active roles in their church communities, promoting acceptance and spirituality. Her commitment serves as a source of inspiration for many to embrace their Catholic Christian Faith and foster a more inclusive Church community.

Currently, she holds the position of Chair of the NAACUS Outreach Committee, where she is responsible for coordinating outreach initiatives designed to enhance participation in NAACUS and promote spiritual growth. She urges African Catholics to participate in NAACUS activities to strengthen ties with parishes, dioceses, and community leaders. Her goals include promoting African Catholic traditions, creating outreach materials, and collaborating with diocesan offices to enhance NAACUS's influence. She is eager to explore collaborative opportunities for the African Catholic community in the United States of America.

ministryCoordinations.name: Celestin Mbuyamba
ministryCoordinations.title: IT Committee Coordinator
ministryCoordinations.bio:
Celestin Mbuyamba is a Congolese immigrant based in the Archdiocese of Saint Paul in Minneapolis-Saint Paul metro area, devoted Catholic, and proud husband and father of four who serves as the IT Committee Coordinator for the National Association of African Catholics in the United States (NAACUS). He is passionate about helping African Catholics across the country connect, grow in faith, and build lasting friendships through a strong and welcoming national community.

In this role, Celestin leads NAACUS digital initiatives, strengthening the website, improving online membership and event registration, expanding communication channels, and ensuring secure, easy-to-use tools for leaders and members. His goal is simple: remove barriers so everyone can participate, stay informed, and feel included, whether you are new to the U.S., raising a family, or looking for a spiritual home and community support.

Professionally, Celestin is a software engineer who enjoys turning big visions into practical solutions. At NAACUS, he brings that same energy to serve the mission.

Celestin invites you to join NAACUS and be part of a growing network of African Catholics united in faith, culture, service, and hope.

ministryCoordinations.name: Mrs Uche Ezechukwu
ministryCoordinations.title: Liturgy Coordinator
ministryCoordinations.bio:
Mrs Uche Ezechukwu is a devoted wife and mom, and the Liturgy Coordinator for the National Association of African Catholics in the United States (NAACUS). In this role, she works to enrich the liturgical experiences of African Catholics across the nation. She is a Healthcare Professional and practices her Christian faith, while focusing on significant effort in supporting her community. She volunteers her time in her local church, leading the Lectors, some cultural organizations and groups for the betterment of her community at large.

Uche with her passion for NAACUS, serves also as one of the Regional coordinators and was part of the Midwestern region during the last regional conference. She has also been with the Liturgy team on many of the national conventions, the yearly African Mass that typically takes place every December and has also participated in the African National Eucharistic Congress (ANEC).

Her dedication to liturgical ministry reflects her deep commitment to celebrating the faith through meaningful worship that honors both her African cultural heritage and Catholic tradition. She also devotes time for advocacy and evangelization with NAACUS mission in mind. Her passion is love of nation, great on nature, her local community and cultural heritage with mentoring of young people, and public speaking engagements.

spiritualAdvisers.name: Rev. Fr. Benoit Mukamba, CSSP
spiritualAdvisers.title: Spiritual Adviser
spiritualAdvisers.bio:
Reverend Benoit Mukamba, CSSp, serves the National Association of African Catholics in the United States as its Spiritual Director, offering pastoral leadership rooted in the Spiritan tradition and guided by a profound commitment to the Church's mission. A native of the Democratic Republic of Congo, he brings more than three decades of priestly ministry shaped by missionary service in East Africa and the United States. His ministry has been marked by a steadfast dedication to evangelization, pastoral care, and the spiritual accompaniment of God's people.

As a custodian of the association's institutional memory, Reverend Mukamba carries a deep understanding of its foundation, development, and ongoing mission. His long-standing involvement provides continuity, clarity of purpose, and a pastoral presence that strengthens the unity of African Catholics across the nation. He holds master's degrees in theology and business administration, a combination that enhances both his pastoral effectiveness and his administrative stewardship.

With a spirit of humility and fidelity to the Gospel, Reverend Mukamba remains devoted to nurturing a vibrant faith community, fostering communion among African Catholics, and guiding the faithful toward a deeper encounter with Christ.

spiritualAdvisers.name: Sr. Joanna Okereke, HHCJ
spiritualAdvisers.title: Spiritual Adviser
spiritualAdvisers.bio:
Sr. Joanna Okereke, HHCJ from Nigeria, is a member of the Congregation of the Handmaids of the Holy Child Jesus. Sr. Joanna is the Assistant Director of the Secretariat of Cultural Diversity in the Church/ Subcommittee on Pastoral Care of Migrants, Refugees, and Travelers/ USCCB.

She is charged with the pastoral care of migrants, refugees, and people on the move communities arriving from foreign lands. She has a wide range of professional work experience in pastoral care, teaching, administration, formation, office and secretarial management. Her professional and work experiences have always been the major source of inspiration, spiritual growth, and social involvement in her life and community. As a community organizer, experience has taught her that effective leadership requires having a clear sense of purpose, certainty of direction and the ability to coordinate in a collaborative manner the activities of the various communities.

She holds a National Certificate in Education from College of Education Awka, Nigeria; a BA in General studies from Northwestern State University, Natchitoches, Louisiana; a MA in Instructional Technology from Edgewood College, Madison, Wisconsin; a MA in Pastoral Theology from St. Joseph’s College of Maine; and a Doctor of Philosophy from Graduate Theological Foundation, Indiana.

spiritualAdvisers.name: Mr. Ntal Alimasi
spiritualAdvisers.title: President Emeritus
spiritualAdvisers.bio:
Ntal Alimasi is one of the Association founding team members and its first President.

He is a former Social Secretary of the African Catholics Association-DMV and currently co-chairs the NAACUS' Advocacy arm.

A cradle Catholic from the DRCongo in a family that boasts an uncle priest, an aunt and a sister nuns, husband and father, Ntal is a parishioner of Saint Augustine Parish in Washington, DC. He led the Parish's Africa & the Diaspora ministry for over two decades, fostering unity and a mutual education and celebration of our Africanity among African American, Caribbean, Afrolatino and African Catholics.

Ntal Alimasi was one of the speakers at the Convocation of Catholic Leaders (Orlando 2017). Known for his work in promoting social justice and community engagement within the Catholic Church, his contributions often emphasize the importance of inclusivity and outreach to marginalized communities.

Outside the Church, Ntal Alimasi is an independent international development consultant with proven expertise in governance and anti-corruption, social and economic community development, and African diaspora networks. He has worked with the World Bank Group, the African Development Bank, USAID, DFID, US Department of State, Belgian Cooperation, UNDP, and various other international organizations and foundations.

Ntal is unapologetically PanAfrican. He speaks English, French, Swahili, Lingala, Mashi, Kinyarwanda, Kirundi, Kikongo, and reads Latin.
